description: MIT component library for Angular 22, and for React 19 starting with the scheduler and the data grid: 29 accessible, signal-based Angular components on native elements, styled by one framework-free stylesheet in CSS cascade layers. Includes a scheduler with resource timelines and repeating events, and a data grid with grouping, tree data and Excel export.
rules: Set up an Angular app with `ng add @needless-ui/angular`, or install @needless-ui/angular, @angular/aria and @angular/cdk and put `@import '@needless-ui/css';` at the top of the global stylesheet.
Import each component from its own entry point, such as `import { NuiButton } from '@needless-ui/angular/button';`, and add it to a standalone component's imports.

In React 19, install @needless-ui/react and @needless-ui/css, put `@import '@needless-ui/css';` in a CSS file of the app, and import the scheduler and the data grid from their entry points, such as `import { NuiGrid } from '@needless-ui/react/grid';`. State is controlled (`sort` with `onSortChange`) or left to the component (`defaultSort`); methods are on the `ref`.
Use the directives on native elements as they are, such as `<button nuiButton>` and `<dialog nuiDialog>`, without wrapping them in other elements to style them.
Components ship no styles: @needless-ui/css styles them inside `@layer nui`, so the app's own CSS overrides it. Theme with `--nui-*` custom properties.
With Tailwind CSS 4, declare `@layer theme, base, nui, components, utilities;` before the imports, so Tailwind's reset can't undo components.
